note: The extensible target-shape patterns corpus (MODERNISER_DESIGN §6.13 / BUILD_PLAN S11). Grow the corpus, not the code. `when_signals` is a predicate over the STRUCTURAL fact stream (consumption booleans + families + disposition + object_kind), so a coarse analyser `modernization_target` never dictates the shape — the structural evidence does. CAP / side-by-side BTP is OUT OF SCOPE (§6.14) and is deliberately absent. Signal grammar: 'consumption:<fact>' | 'hint:<hint>' | 'rule:<analyser_rule_id>' | 'family:<family>' | 'disposition:<d>' | 'target:<t>' | 'object_kind:<k>', combined via all/any/none.

patterns.name: Headless RAP Business Object
patterns.example: abap_fico batch posting program — a transactional backend BO (CDS + managed RAP BO + DCL); no OData service, no Fiori metadata.

patterns.name: RAP Business Object exposed as an OData V4 service
patterns.example: a function consumed remotely (RFC/BAPI) — a RAP BO exposed as an OData V4 service; no interactive Fiori UI.

patterns.name: RAP Business Object with a Fiori Elements UI
patterns.example: an ALV grid / dynpro maintenance screen — a RAP BO with an OData service and a Fiori Elements list/object page. The UI evidence arrives from a CPG edge (ui_salv/ui_dynpro) OR from the analyser's screen RULES: a dynpro is a screen, not a call, so it leaves no edge for the consumption detector to see. The rules are used rather than the coarser `ui_rearch` hint because that hint also fires on a WRITE list, which is batch output and stays headless.

patterns.name: Event-driven RAP Business Object (RAP business events)
patterns.example: an IDoc / ALE inbound flow — a RAP BO raising/consuming RAP business events for the asynchronous integration.

patterns.name: Analytical CDS model
patterns.example: a reporting / aggregation program — an analytical CDS cube + query (@Analytics.dataCategory). The `none` guard is why a config/DDIC table is not handed an analytical model on the strength of the analyser's coarse `CDS View Entity` target alone: a shape is never justified on silence. The query publishes data, so it carries an authorization contract like every other exposing shape.

patterns.name: Value-help CDS view
patterns.example: a classic search help / F4 — a value-help CDS view with @Consumption.valueHelpDefinition.

patterns.name: Custom entity + query provider
patterns.example: a function reading external / non-persisted data — a custom entity backed by a query-provider class.

patterns.name: Adopt a released SAP standard (fit-to-standard)
patterns.example: an area S/4 already delivers as a released app/API — wire to the standard instead of building bespoke (fit-to-standard).
